Before the time being spoken about — Anterior / previo/a.
An earlier version of the report was lost.
Making someone feel ashamed or uncomfortable — Embarazoso/a / bochornoso/a.
Beside awkward. Verb: embarrass. Noun: embarrassment. False friend: embarazada in Spanish means pregnant.
Stop; come to a finish — Terminar / acabar.
The last part, noun — Final / fin.
I liked the end of the book.
Very bad in a deep, deliberate way — Malvado/a / maligno/a.
An evil man ran the prison.
He wrote about good and evil.
Look at something closely — Examinar / inspeccionar.
v|Beside probe and explore. Noun: examination.
Force someone to live away from their country — Desterrar / exiliar.
The writer was exiled for ten years.
Someone who lives away from home, noun — Exiliado/a / desterrado/a.
Think something will happen — Esperar / prever.
Believe someone should do something — Esperar de.
They expect us to arrive early.
v|Beside anticipate. Careful: expect is to think, wait means to stay until.
Say or show what you feel — Expresar / manifestar.
Far from what is usual or moderate — Extremo/a / radical.
Beside excessive and radical. Adverb: extremely.
Things known to be true — Hechos / datos.
Give me the facts, not your opinion.
Beside data. Singular: fact. Phrase: in fact.
The roof of the barn fell in.
v|Beside collapse. Not separable. Different from fall in love and fall in with.
Work something out with numbers — Calcular.
A number or amount, noun — Cifra.
The shape of a person's body — Figura / tipo.
v|Beside calculate. Phrase: figure out, meaning understand.
Come to the end of something — Terminar / acabar.
I finished the book last night.
v|Beside conclude. Pattern: finish doing something, never finish to do.
Right for a purpose — Apto/a / adecuado/a.
The water is not fit to drink.
Be the right size — Quedar bien / caber.
These shoes do not fit me.
Water covering land that is usually dry — Inundación / riada.
v|Beside torrent. Note the spelling: it rhymes with blood.
Go after someone or something — Seguir.
Do what you are told — Seguir / obedecer.
Beside subsequent. Also a preposition: following the meeting.
Showing poor judgement; silly — Insensato/a / tonto/a.
It was foolish to lend him the car.
Beside absurd. Noun: fool. Adverb: foolishly.
Make someone do something — Forzar / obligar.
Hunger forced them to sell the farm.
v|Beside compel. Pattern: force someone to do something.
The ability to see what will be needed — Previsión.
He had the foresight to book early.
Beside precaution. Opposite: hindsight, seeing clearly afterwards.
Let someone or something go — Liberar / soltar.
Causing fear or shock — Espantoso/a / horroroso/a.
There was a frightful noise upstairs.
Beside horrid. Verb: frighten. Adverb: frightfully.
Bring the eyebrows together in anger or worry — Fruncir el ceño.
v|Beside scowl. Phrase: frown on something, to disapprove of it.
We had great fun at the beach.
Beside jest. Uncountable: a lot of fun, not a fun. Phrase: make fun of someone.
Of the deepest, most basic kind — Fundamental / esencial.
There is a fundamental difference between them.
Where did you get that coat?
v|Beside obtain. Irregular: gets, got, got or gotten.
Move smoothly and without effort — Deslizarse.
The boat glided along the canal.
v|Beside skim. Verb: glide; glides, glided, glided.
Please go on with your story.
v|Beside resume. Not separable. Pattern: go on doing something.
Travelling here and there — Yendo de un lado a otro.
He spent the year going around Asia.
Spreading from person to person — Circulando / rondando.
There is a bad cold going around.
Beside abroad. From the phrasal verb go around.
The quality of being good — Bondad.
She believes in the goodness of people.
The good part of food — Lo bueno / los nutrientes.
Boiling takes the goodness out of vegetables.
They live in a grand old house.
Beside majestic. Careful: grand is impressive, big is only large.
Feel deep sadness, especially after a death — Afligirse / llorar una pérdida.
She is still grieving for her mother.
Person who protects a place or people — Guardia / guardián.
A guard stood at the gate.
Protect or watch over — Vigilar / custodiar.
Give an answer without being sure — Adivinar / suponer.
An answer given that way, noun — Suposición / conjetura.
Something that takes place — Suceso / acontecimiento.
It was the strangest happening of the week.
Being cruel or severe — Dureza / severidad.
The harshness of the sentence shocked us.
Dislike someone or something very strongly — Odiar / detestar.
I hate getting up in the dark.
His eyes were full of hate.
Taking no notice of danger or advice — Despreocupado/a / que no hace caso.
Heedless of the cold, he went out in shirtsleeves.
Beside reckless. Verb: heed. Pattern: heedless of something.
Put something where it cannot be found — Esconder / ocultar.
She hid the key under a stone.
Go where you cannot be seen — Esconderse.
The cat hides behind the sofa.
v|Beside conceal. Irregular: hides, hid, hidden.
Keep a feeling from showing — Contener / reprimir.
Keep something inside a space — Retener / encerrar.
The dam holds in the water.
v|Beside confine. Separable: hold it in.
Connected with God or religion — Santo/a / sagrado/a.
Put your arms round someone — Abrazar.
v|Beside embrace. Doubles the g: hugged, hugging.
They live in a huge house.
Beside enormous and vast. Adverb: hugely.
Beside hasty. Verb: hurry. Adverb: hurriedly.
Having power or influence — Importante / destacado/a.
Beside prominent and urgent. Noun: importance.
Facts told or learnt about something — Información.
I need more information about the course.
Beside data. Uncountable: a piece of information, never an information.
He was found insane at the trial.
Driving in this fog is insane.
Beside lunatic. Noun: insanity. The first sense is a legal term; say mentally ill in ordinary speech.
Very serious and deeply felt — Intenso/a / apasionado/a.
She has an intense interest in music.
Beside keen. Noun: intensity. Careful: intense describes the thing, intensive means thorough.
The wish to know more about something — Interés.
She has an interest in old films.
Money paid for a loan — Intereses.
Make someone want to know more — Interesar.
Make something that did not exist before — Inventar.
Make up a story that is not true — Inventarse.
Try to find out the truth about something — Investigar.
Make something likely to happen — Provocar / buscarse.
Leaving the door open invites trouble.
The feeling of fearing to lose someone, or wanting what another has — Celos / envidia.
Something said to make people laugh — Chiste / broma.
A decision made by a court — Fallo / sentencia.
The ability to decide sensibly — Juicio / criterio.
Beside verdict. Also spelt judgement in British English.
Continue to have something — Quedarse con / conservar.
I keep the tools in the shed.
He keeps asking the same question.
v|Beside maintain and retain. Irregular: keeps, kept, kept.
Make someone stay inside — No dejar salir / retener.
The teacher kept in the whole class.
Hold a feeling back — Contener / guardarse.
Do not keep in your worries.
v|Beside confine. Separable: keep them in.
Like a king; fit for a king — Regio/a / majestuoso/a.
Beside majestic. More common today: royal, regal.
